questions.question: Who is the king of the Greek gods?
questions.fact: Zeus ruled from Mount Olympus, Greece's highest mountain, and threw thunderbolts when angry.

questions.question: Who is the Greek god of the sea?
questions.fact: Poseidon carried a three-pronged spear called a trident and was also the god of earthquakes and horses.

questions.question: Who rules the underworld in Greek myth?
questions.fact: Hades wasn't evil in Greek myths; he was strict but fair. The Romans called him Pluto.

questions.question: What is Zeus called by the Romans?
questions.fact: The planet Jupiter is named after him, fittingly, as it's the biggest planet.

questions.question: What is Poseidon called by the Romans?
questions.fact: The planet Neptune was named in 1846, and its deep blue colour turned out to suit the sea god.

questions.question: Who is the Greek goddess of love?
questions.fact: Aphrodite was said to have been born from the sea foam near Cyprus.

questions.question: What is Aphrodite called by the Romans?
questions.fact: Venus is the brightest planet in the night sky, which suits the goddess of beauty.

questions.question: Who is the Greek goddess of wisdom?
questions.fact: Athens is named after Athena, who won the city by giving it the olive tree.

questions.question: Which Greek hero could only be hurt in his heel?
questions.fact: Achilles's mother dipped him in the River Styx to make him invulnerable, holding him by the heel.

questions.question: Who cut off Medusa's head?
questions.fact: Perseus used a shiny shield as a mirror, so he never had to look directly at Medusa.

questions.question: What happened to people who looked at Medusa?
questions.fact: Even after her head was cut off, Medusa's gaze could still turn people to stone.

questions.question: Which hero performed twelve labours?
questions.fact: One of Hercules's labours was cleaning huge stables in one day. He did it by changing the course of two rivers.

questions.question: Who flew too close to the sun on wings made of wax?
questions.fact: Icarus's father, Daedalus, made the wings to escape Crete and warned him not to fly too high or too low.

questions.question: Which half-man, half-bull creature lived in the Labyrinth?
questions.fact: The Labyrinth was built by Daedalus, the same inventor who made Icarus's wings.

questions.question: Who killed the Minotaur?
questions.fact: Princess Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could find his way out of the Labyrinth.

questions.question: A centaur is half human and half…
questions.fact: Chiron was the wise centaur who trained heroes like Achilles and Jason.

questions.question: What is special about a cyclops?
questions.fact: Odysseus escaped the cyclops Polyphemus by telling him his name was "Nobody".

questions.question: Who stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans?
questions.fact: Zeus punished Prometheus by chaining him to a rock, where an eagle ate his liver every day, and it grew back each night.

questions.question: Which Titan was made to hold up the sky?
questions.fact: The Atlantic Ocean and the Atlas Mountains are named after him, and a book of maps is called an "atlas".

questions.question: What came out when Pandora opened her jar?
options: All the evils of the world
questions.fact: The original story mentions a jar, not a box. "Pandora's box" came from a mistranslation centuries later.

questions.question: What was left inside Pandora's jar?
questions.fact: Today, "opening Pandora's box" means starting something that causes lots of unexpected problems.

questions.question: Which hero sailed with the Argonauts to find the Golden Fleece?
questions.fact: Jason's ship was the Argo, which is why its crew were called the Argonauts.

questions.question: How long did Odysseus's journey home from Troy take?
questions.fact: The Trojan War itself lasted 10 years, and then Odysseus's journey home took another 10.

questions.question: How did the Greeks get inside the city of Troy?
questions.fact: Today a "Trojan" is also malicious software that pretends to be harmless, just like the wooden horse.

questions.question: Who is the Norse god of thunder?
questions.fact: Marvel's Thor is blond, but in the Norse myths Thor was usually described with a red beard.

questions.question: What is Thor's hammer called?
questions.fact: Only the worthy can lift Mjölnir in the Marvel films. In the myths, the hammer always returned to Thor's hand.

questions.question: Who is the chief of the Norse gods?
questions.fact: Odin gave up one of his eyes to drink from a well of wisdom.

questions.question: Which Norse god is the trickster?
questions.fact: Loki could change shape. In one myth he turned into a mare and gave birth to Sleipnir.

questions.question: What is the great hall for fallen Viking warriors called?
questions.fact: Valkyries chose which warriors died in battle and took half of them to Valhalla.

questions.question: What is the rainbow bridge in Norse myth called?
questions.fact: Bifröst is said to burn with fire, so giants can't cross it into Asgard.

questions.question: What is the giant tree that connects the Norse worlds called?
questions.fact: Yggdrasil is usually described as a giant ash tree, holding the nine worlds together.

questions.question: What is Ragnarök?
options: The end of the world in Norse myth
questions.fact: In Ragnarök, many gods die, but the world rises again from the sea, fresh and green.

questions.question: How many legs does Odin's horse Sleipnir have?
questions.fact: Sleipnir was the fastest horse of all and could ride through the air and over the sea.

questions.question: Which day of the week is named after Thor?
questions.fact: Friday is named after the goddess Frigg (or Freya) and Wednesday after Odin, also called Woden.

questions.question: Which Egyptian god had the head of a jackal?
questions.fact: Anubis watched over the dead and mummification. Jackals were often seen near ancient cemeteries.

questions.question: Who was the Egyptian sun god?
questions.fact: Ra was believed to sail across the sky in a boat every day and through the underworld every night.

questions.question: Which Egyptian god had the head of a falcon?
questions.fact: The "Eye of Horus" was a popular Egyptian symbol of protection and good health.

questions.question: The Egyptian goddess Bastet was shown as a…
questions.fact: Cats were loved in ancient Egypt. Many were mummified, and harming one could be severely punished.

questions.question: In Egyptian belief, what was weighed against a feather after death?
questions.fact: If the heart was heavier than the feather of truth, a monster called Ammit ate it.

questions.question: Which legendary king pulled a sword from a stone?
questions.fact: In some versions of the legend, Excalibur was a different sword, given to Arthur by the Lady of the Lake.

questions.question: What is King Arthur's sword called?
questions.fact: When Arthur was dying, Excalibur was thrown back into a lake, where a hand caught it.

questions.question: Which wizard helped King Arthur?
questions.fact: In some stories, Merlin lives backwards in time, which is how he knows the future.

questions.question: Which legendary outlaw lived in Sherwood Forest?
questions.fact: Robin Hood stories date back to at least the 1300s. Sherwood Forest is near Nottingham, England.

questions.question: Which Swiss hero shot an apple off his son's head?
questions.fact: Rossini's opera "William Tell" has one of the most famous overtures ever, often used for galloping scenes.

questions.question: What is the Loch Ness Monster's nickname?
questions.fact: The famous 1934 "surgeon's photo" of Nessie was later revealed to be a toy submarine with a model head.

questions.question: What is the Yeti also called?
questions.fact: "Yeti" comes from the Sherpa language of the Himalayas. In North America, a similar creature is called Bigfoot.

questions.question: Which creature drinks blood and is scared of garlic?
questions.fact: Bram Stoker's Dracula (1897) made vampires famous, though vampire legends are much older.

questions.question: Which creature changes shape at the full moon?
questions.fact: The idea that werewolves can only be killed by silver bullets became popular mainly through films.

questions.question: Which mythical bird is reborn from its own ashes?
questions.fact: According to the legend, only one phoenix lives at a time, and it lives for around 500 years.

questions.question: A griffin has the body of a lion and the head of…
questions.fact: Griffins were said to guard treasure, especially gold.

questions.question: What is a mermaid?
questions.fact: Columbus reported seeing "mermaids" in 1493. They were most likely manatees.

questions.question: In Greek myth, which creatures lured sailors to their doom with songs?
questions.fact: Odysseus had his crew plug their ears with wax and tie him to the mast so he could hear the Sirens safely.

questions.question: How many Muses were there in Greek mythology?
questions.fact: The Muses inspired the arts. Our words "music" and "museum" come from them.

questions.question: Which Greek god is the messenger with winged sandals?
questions.fact: Hermes was also the god of travellers, thieves and luck. The Romans called him Mercury.

questions.question: Who is the Greek god of wine and parties?
questions.fact: The Romans called Dionysus "Bacchus". Wild parties were once called "bacchanals".

questions.question: Who is the Greek god of war?
questions.fact: Ares wasn't very popular even among the Greek gods. Athena was the goddess of wise battle strategy.

questions.question: Mars was the Roman god of…
questions.fact: The month of March and the planet Mars are both named after the Roman god of war.

questions.question: What is the Santa Compaña in Galician legend?
options: A night procession of lost souls
questions.fact: In Galician legend, the Santa Compaña walks at night carrying candles, led by a living person who can't stop.

questions.question: Which goddess of Basque mythology is said to live in caves on mountain tops?
questions.fact: Mari is said to control the weather, and she lives in caves on mountains like Anboto.

questions.question: What is a "duende" in Spanish folklore?
questions.fact: In Spanish, someone with "duende" has a magical, hard-to-explain charm, especially in flamenco.

questions.question: Who fell in love with his own reflection in Greek myth?
questions.fact: Narcissus gave his name to the narcissus flower (daffodil) and to the word "narcissist".

questions.question: Who went into the underworld to bring back his wife Eurydice?
questions.fact: Orpheus could bring Eurydice back if he didn't look back. He did, just before they reached the surface.

questions.question: What is the name of the three-headed dog guarding the underworld?
questions.fact: Cerberus is usually shown with three heads. Hercules captured him as his last labour.
